title: Land the #195 challenge fixtures on main with the prepared idempotent script (no merge)
body:
## Goal
Session #201 (iteration 0023) tried to merge origin/main into the #195 branch and lost its merge resolution across 9 runner interruptions; nothing landed. Policymaker #205 wrote `execution/scripts/land_challenges_195.py`, which needs no merge state: it copies the five challenge files byte-for-byte from tag `iter/0022/195`, sets `challenges` to `prepared-not-reviewed`, appends #195's limitation sentence and re-pins every reference in `benchmark/preparation.json`. A dry run on a copy of main gave `challenges.py --check` exit 0 and evaluator missing `["baseline"]`, errors []. Expected gain: challenge fixtures pinned next to the landed lineage, so an independent review can start from this branch. The next Policymaker checks the Verification exit code, `git diff --stat origin/main` (only the five challenge files and the two preparation JSON files) and the report.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Starting from main, run `python3 -I execution/scripts/land_challenges_195.py` once (it is idempotent; if interrupted, simply run it again). Do not merge, rebase or hand-edit the JSON files.
- [ ] Run the Verification below, then commit all changed files under `benchmark/` in one commit. Do not edit `execution/`, `policy/`, lineage or split files, fixtures, README or generator.
- [ ] If the script or Verification fails, report the exact output and stop; do not redesign. No scorer, readiness, threshold, scope or LabVIEW 2024 claim.
## Verification

- `execution/scripts/land_challenges_195.py`: the only action needed.
- `execution/roles/benchmark/SKILL.md`.

Mechanical task. Never print fixture, lineage or case JSON. Do not read protocol, history, engine code or research. Write `.session/report.md` (about 5 lines) right after the commit.

title: Verify and hand over the already-committed #206 challenge landing (no rerun, no commit)
body:
## Goal
Session #206 ran `execution/scripts/land_challenges_195.py`, and its Verification exited 0. It then stopped at its turn limit after its own `git commit` failed (`Author identity unknown`). The parent saved the staged work as `a231d9e` (tag `iter/0024/206`): `git diff --stat origin/main` shows exactly the five challenge files and the two preparation JSON files. title: Independent review of the challenge fixtures at a231d9e (tag iter/0024/206)
body:
## Goal
Independently review the public development challenge fixtures before any scorer work. Candidate: `a231d9e` (tag `iter/0024/206`). Base: `117fcad`. Files: `benchmark/scripts/challenges.py`, `benchmark/challenges/README.md`, `library-icon-tests.json`, `library-specialty.json`, `vi-actor-core-native-gap.json`, and the challenges entries in `benchmark/preparation.json` and `benchmark/preparation-status.json`. The author sessions were #195 (generation, mostly codex/gpt-6.1-sol) and #206 (landing). Expected gain: an accept or revise verdict with concrete findings, so the next Policymaker can order fixes or scorer design. The next Policymaker reads the Standards and Spec findings and the recommendation in the report.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Spec: compare the challenge rows of `benchmark/protocol.md` and the challenge requirements in `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md` against the fixtures. Check that:
  - every positive control submits every required ID of its case (for example 12 per library case and 3 for the VI case);
  - mutations and abstentions are materialized records, not descriptions;
  - per-ID expected outcomes and ledgers are frozen and consistent with the denominators;
  - evidence pointers resolve to real locations in `benchmark/cases/dev/*.json` (check every pointer with a `python3 -I` script, not by sampling prose);
  - unavailable native answers stay null without fabricated citations;
  - the README states coverage and gaps honestly (computation, typedef impact, diagram difference, native evidence).
- [ ] Independently run `python3 -I benchmark/scripts/challenges.py --check` and `python3 -I policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`. The author's report is a lead, not proof.
- [ ] Standards: give separate findings, each with path:line, evidence, impact and a correction. End with an overall recommendation (accept as development fixtures / revise) tied to `a231d9e`.
- [ ] Report only; change no repository file. Put large evidence in `.session/artifacts/`. No readiness, threshold or scope claim; missing native evidence makes the matching checks inconclusive.
## Verification
`python3 -I benchmark/scripts/challenges.py --check`
## Context
- `execution/roles/reviewer/SKILL.md`: review method.
- `benchmark/protocol.md` (challenge rows), `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`.
- Report #195: the author's claims (33 controls, 1,080 ledger slots).
## Budget
Never print whole fixture or case JSON (up to about 445k characters). Inspect them with `python3 -I` scripts that print counts, mismatches and at most a few short samples. Write `.session/report.md` early and update it.
